headline: High: shared write/network surfaces and MCP/tooling create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors between Dify and LightAgent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write filesystem and uses tools wired into agent/workflow flows; LightAgent exposes MCP over stdio/SSE and runtime hooks that can observe or replace lifecycle payloads. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if outputs are passed between them, though no direct shared channel is documented.
conditions: IF Dify workflow outputs are forwarded into LightAgent tool prompts or MCP payloads
IF LightAgent runtime hooks or MCP handlers parse Dify-generated text as instructions
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter/schema between agent outputs and tool prompts
Disable automatic tool execution on untrusted text
Require provenance tags on all inter-agent messages
Review MCP handlers for instruction-following behavior
requires-engineering: add content sanitization and allowlist parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches knowledge base content, conversation logs, model provider keys, and tool credentials; LightAgent touches conversations, long-term memory, trace data, tool results, and workflow state. Both have broad network egress, so if they share a workspace or exchange artifacts, sensitive data can flow across the pair in default-like deployments.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed against the same workspace or datastore
IF Dify knowledge-base files or logs are exposed to LightAgent inputs
IF LightAgent forwards trace data or tool results to external APIs
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials per agent
Restrict file sharing to explicit exports only
Turn off verbose trace/log export
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify has filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and broad egress; LightAgent has broad egress, browsers, subprocesses, and MCP. If both operate on the same mutable resources or shared workflow state, concurrent writes or conflicting tool actions are plausible. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or shared workflow state
IF both are allowed to invoke side-effecting tools concurrently
IF no external lock or queue serializes their actions
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories and credentials
Serialize side-effecting steps through one queue
Disable concurrent writes during shared runs
Use file locks for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestration-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an orchestration platform that can emit agent/workflow outputs, while LightAgent supports tool calling and runtime hooks that can replace lifecycle payloads. If LightAgent treats Dify output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream actions without verification, and the pair has enough automation to make the blast radius operationally significant.
conditions: IF LightAgent consumes Dify-generated text as a decision input
IF downstream tools act on that text without human or rule-based verification
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any action-taking tool
Require citations or structured outputs from Dify
Block direct execution of free-form agent text
Log and review all high-impact actions
requires-engineering: add policy gates for tool execution

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly touches conversation logs, knowledge-base content, and secrets; LightAgent touches long-term memory, trace data, workflow state, and provenance metadata. The profiles show different retention-sensitive surfaces but no documented residency or certification alignment, so a compliance mismatch is plausible and should be treated as medium rather than assumed absent.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Dify logs or knowledge bases
IF LightAgent retains traces or memory longer than the operator's policy
IF either deployment crosses a residency boundary without a DPA
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent
Set explicit retention limits on logs and traces
Disable storage of regulated fields in memory
Confirm residency and DPA terms for both deployments
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention enforcement
